original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The Financial Times reported that OpenAI and Google supplied AI-model access to Singapore-based subsidiaries of Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent, whose parent firms were on a U.S. defence list; the report described the sales as legal under the rules then in force.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Cross-border access restrictions must be grounded in an applicable rule and preserve the governed actor, jurisdiction and service scope. A parent-company designation alone does not establish that lawful subsidiary access violated or exceeded a restriction.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The preserved reporting says these sales were lawful under the rules then in force and does not identify a sovereign access restriction propagated by the service provider beyond its established jurisdiction, actor or function.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The reporting said OpenAI later suspended Alibaba-affiliated users because it suspected model distillation; the preserved accounts do not identify which entity performed extraction, the extent of any extraction, or the specific rule supporting the suspension.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A consequential access restriction should be based on attributable conduct and a reviewable rule, with the affected users and scope tied to the evidence supporting the action.
